rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report the authors' own UAV multispectral flights (Phantom 4, DJI multispectral camera) over rosemary and sage in Grotte, Sicily, NDVI and TCARI/OSAVI maps (Figures 3-4), a drying trial with sensor logging (Figure 5) and microbiological plate counts (Figure 6).
rows.notes: The study uses UAV multispectral imagery (NDVI, TCARI/OSAVI) only to assess canopy vigor/greenness and pick the harvest date of rosemary and sage. No thermal imaging, no water-stress index, no irrigation scheduling and no water-use measurement are reported. It therefore only supports the canopy-vigor/chlorophyll-mapping precondition of the passage, not the irrigation-scheduling or water-conservation effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report own UAV flights, index maps, drying and microbiological data. Q2: Section 2.4 and 3.1 (Figure 3) - UAV multispectral NDVI time series were used to decide harvest time; rosemary harvested when most plants reached NDVI 0.64 with flowering confirmed visually, sage harvested at NDVI 0.59; Figure 4 shows TCARI/OSAVI and NDVI maps of rosemary, oregano and sage rows used to assess canopy vigor/chlorophyll.
rows.notes: Support is limited to the harvest-timing and canopy-vigor part of the passage; the study has no thermal sensing, no precision irrigation or nutrient-management workflow, and no water-use-efficiency or yield data. Harvest timing was determined from NDVI thresholds plus visual flowering checks, with no quantitative validation, no measured chlorophyll, no replication statistics for the indices. The claimed TCARI/OSAVI-chlorophyll relationship relies on cited work (Haboudane et al.), not own measurements. Single farm field in one season; limitations stated (MCARI sensitivity to background at low LAI) are cited, not the study's own.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report own field, drying and laboratory data.
rows.notes: No CWSI, no thermal imaging, no irrigation scheduling and no water-saving figures appear anywhere in the study. The technologies actually tested are UAV multispectral vegetation indices for harvest timing and a photovoltaic smart solar dryer with WSN monitoring, not irrigation scheduling apps or CWSI-guided scheduling.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.6 and 3.1-3.3 report own field, drying and laboratory data.
rows.notes: The study contains no deficit-irrigation treatments, no CWSI scheduling, no phenolic or metabolite analyses and no biomass-yield response to water. Its own results concern NDVI-based harvest timing, drying-chamber humidity/temperature profiles, final moisture content (15% sage, 17% rosemary) and microbial counts before/after drying, none of which bear on CWSI-guided irrigation or phenolic concentration.

notes: Full text appears complete though some pages are duplicated/garbled by layout overlap. The study is a single-farm case study in Grotte (Sicily) combining UAV multispectral index mapping for harvest timing of rosemary and sage, a photovoltaic smart solar dryer with wireless sensor monitoring, and microbiological assessment of fresh vs dried herbs. It contains nothing on irrigation, water stress, thermal imaging, CWSI or water savings; the irrigation-related claims cite it without support.
